findings.title: requireNonNull checks the wrong argument (rawTokenId is not validated)
findings.body: The constructor does `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. Since `grantType` was already validated on the preceding line, this duplicate call is a no-op and does NOT enforce the intended non-null constraint on `rawTokenId`. The instance will then be created with a null rawTokenId and the field assigned. Any subsequent use of `getRawTokenId()` will return null and break token ID encoding/decoding (e.g. a token could be encoded with an embedded null) or surface as a cryptic NPE later.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has both an off-by-one and an inverted condition
findings.body:
Two bugs in the new matcher body:
```
if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
```
1. Off-by-one: the grant type is the last 2 characters of the 6-char prefix, i.e. indices 4 and 5. The call must be `items[0].substring(4, 6)`. The current call returns a mix of the second char of token type and the first char of grant type, not the grant type alone.
2. Inverted condition: the matcher is supposed to SUCCESS only when the grant type matches the expected shortcut, but the code returns false (no match) when the substring equals the expected shortcut. A correct version would be: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
As written, the matcher effectively accepts any well-formed encoded token ID regardless of which grant produced it, so integration tests that rely on it (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) will not be able to detect regressions in grant type encoding.

findings.title: Public copy constructor on Context was removed without replacement
findings.body: The diff deletes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor that was part of the public static nested class `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Any external code (custom grant type providers) that currently uses this constructor will fail to compile against this SPI. The PR description does not mention this removal. If the constructor was genuinely unused, leave it intact or annotate it `@Deprecated` so existing implementations still compile.

findings.title: New required method getShortcut() breaks external OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `String getShortcut()` is added to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI without a default and without `@Deprecated` overloads. Any external implementation of this factory interface (custom grant providers) compiled against a previous Keycloak version will throw `NoSuchMethodError`/`AbstractMethodError` at startup because the bytecode references the missing interface method. Even when re-compiled, the change is not source-compatible unless each implementer explicitly returns a constant. Consider providing a default that returns a value derived from `getId()` (e.g. first two unique letters) so that existing implementations keep working, or document the upgrade requirement prominently.

findings.title: Access token `jti` now encodes grant type, session type and lightweight flag visible to clients
findings.body: `initToken` now sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, which prepends a 6-character prefix (e.g. `onrtac:`) to the UUID used as the JWT `jti` and as `Details.TOKEN_ID`. The prefix reveals to any party that sees the access token (resource servers, browser-side apps, logs, error reports) the grant type that minted the token (including `pre-authorized_code`, `token-exchange`, etc.), whether the session is offline/online/transient, and whether the token is a lightweight access token. While not secret, this leaks behaviour (e.g. presence of offline sessions, use of token exchange) that is otherwise not conveyed to clients and that may not be desirable in all deployments (e.g. compliance, fingerprinting of Keycloak version/features, ability to distinguish realms/configurations). Consider making the SPI opt-in or at least allowing operators to disable it, and documenting the information disclosure in release notes.

findings.title: Unused import TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory
findings.body: The diff adds `import org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory;` but the new line uses `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` instead of any constant from `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory`. The import is dead and should be removed to keep the file clean and avoid IDE warnings.

findings.title: No tests for the new SPI wiring in production token issuance
findings.body: The unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` only exercises the encoder's encode/decode logic with a manually-seeded factory map. There is no test that drives the full token issuance path (e.g. an authorization code, refresh, CIBA or device flow integration test) and asserts on the actual token ID prefix, nor is there a test that runs `postInit` against a real `KeycloakSessionFactory` to validate the shortcut-uniqueness assertion in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` (i.e. detecting duplicate shortcuts across grant factories). Combined with the broken AssertEvents matcher (#2), this means the PR can regress grant-type encoding in production without any test catching it.

findings.title: Constants.GRANT_TYPE key collides with OAuth2 form parameter name
findings.body: `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is defined as `OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, which is the literal string `"grant_type"` (the standard OAuth2 form parameter name). It is used both as the form-parameter key to populate `OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType` and as the attribute key on `ClientSessionContext`. Because session context attributes and form parameters are different objects, this is not a runtime bug, but the shared string is a sharp edge: any code that reads or writes `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on the wrong object (e.g. on the form params) would be confused. Use a distinct namespaced key such as `Constants.GRANT_TYPE + ".attribute"` or move it to a session-context-specific constant to make the distinction explicit.
